content.title: About
content.content: Pupusas with beans are a traditional Latin American dish consisting of thick corn‑maize tortillas stuffed with cooked black beans. They are often served with salsa, sour cream, or tomato sauce. This hearty street‑food staple is popular in El Salvador and throughout Central America.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pupusas originated in El Salvador in the early 20th century and quickly became a national symbol.
The dough is traditionally made from fermented corn masa, giving the tortillas a subtle tang.
Bean filling is usually simmered with garlic, onion, and spices, and sometimes mixed with cheese or chicharrón (fried pork fat).
There are more than 30 filling variations, ranging from cheese and spinach to seafood and meat.
Pupusas are often cooked on an open grill (parilla), where they develop a lightly crisped exterior.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Beans and corn masa together provide a complete set of amino acids beneficial for muscle repair and maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber from the beans supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn masa releases energy slowly, helping maintain stable glucose levels.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation, nerve function, and muscle tone.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared without excessive added fat, pupusas remain a relatively light meal.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the corn starch used in the dough.

items.title: Sodium in sauces
items.content: Traditional accompaniments can be salty; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Possible bacterial contamination
items.content: If the beans are not fully cooked, there is a risk of bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pupusas are typically enjoyed hot, split open and topped with salsa, sour cream, guacamole, or tomato sauce. They can be served as a main dish or alongside rice and salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pupusas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. They can be frozen after cooling and reheated in an oven or on a grill.
